one_liner: In 2019, {{n:attr}} deaths were attributable to bacterial AMR and {{n:assoc}} were associated with it.
one_liner_plain: Bacterial antimicrobial resistance was a leading cause of death worldwide in 2019

citation.title: Global burden of bacterial antimicrobial resistance in 2019: a systematic analysis
citation.authors: Antimicrobial Resistance Collaborators; Murray CJL, Ikuta KS, Sharara F, et al.

sections.background: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is often described as a looming threat, but earlier estimates covered only specific pathogen-drug combinations in a few places. Without a global number, AMR was hard to compare with HIV, malaria, or heart disease when governments set priorities. This Global Burden of Disease analysis set out to produce the most comprehensive estimate yet of how many deaths bacterial AMR causes, where, and from which bugs and drugs.

methods.design: Systematic analysis and predictive statistical modelling within the Global Burden of Disease framework; not a trial.
methods.scope: 23 pathogens and 88 pathogen-drug combinations in {{n:countries}} countries and territories, for the year 2019.
methods.data: Systematic literature reviews, hospital systems, surveillance systems, and other sources: {{n:records}} individual records or isolates and 7585 study-location-years. Models filled in locations with no data.
methods.two_counterfactuals: Attributable deaths: compared with a world where drug-resistant infections were replaced by drug-susceptible ones. Associated deaths: compared with a world where drug-resistant infections were replaced by no infection at all.
methods.model_chain: Deaths where infection played a role, then the share by infectious syndrome, then by pathogen, then the share resistant to each antibiotic, then the excess risk of death from that resistance.
methods.uncertainty: 95% uncertainty intervals from 1000 posterior draws; models cross-validated for out-of-sample predictive validity.

sections.results: An estimated {{n:assoc}} deaths were associated with bacterial AMR in 2019, including {{n:attr}} deaths directly attributable to it (95% UI 0.911 to 1.71 million). Measured by associated deaths, AMR would have been the third leading cause of death in 2019, behind only ischaemic heart disease and stroke. Even by the stricter attributable measure it would have ranked 12th, ahead of both HIV and malaria. The burden was uneven. The death rate attributable to resistance was highest in western sub-Saharan Africa ({{n:high}} per 100 000) and lowest in Australasia ({{n:low}} per 100 000). Lower respiratory infections were the most burdensome syndrome, with more than {{n:lri}} deaths associated with resistance. A handful of bugs did most of the damage. Six pathogens (E. coli, S. aureus, K. pneumoniae, S. pneumoniae, A. baumannii, and P. aeruginosa) accounted for {{n:six}} of attributable deaths. One pathogen-drug pair, methicillin-resistant S. aureus (MRSA), alone caused more than {{n:mrsa}} attributable deaths.
sections.conclusions: This study provides the first comprehensive assessment of the global burden of bacterial AMR. AMR is a leading cause of death around the world, with the highest burdens in low-resource settings, and a small number of pathogen-drug combinations drive most of it.
sections.limitations: Data were sparse in many low- and middle-income countries, so estimates there lean heavily on modelling. There is no universal laboratory standard for resistance, and breakpoints changed over time, so classification was heterogeneous. Passive surveillance may overestimate resistance if cultures are drawn mainly after treatment fails, and hospital data in LMICs may skew toward urban or sicker patients. Community- and hospital-acquired infections could not be separated well.
sections.practice_impact: GBD AMR turned AMR from an abstract warning into a ranked cause of death, giving policy makers a number on par with HIV and malaria. It is now the standard citation for AMR's scale in global policy, and it points stewardship, vaccines, infection prevention, and new-drug efforts at the pathogens and regions that matter most.

numbers.label: Countries and territories
numbers.source_quote: We estimated deaths and disability-adjusted life-years (DALYs) attributable to and associated with bacterial AMR for 23 pathogens and 88 pathogen–drug combinations in 204 countries and territories in 2019.

numbers.label: Deaths associated with bacterial AMR (millions)
numbers.source_quote: there were an estimated 4.95 million (3.62–6.57) deaths associated with bacterial AMR in 2019, including 1.27 million (95% UI 0.911–1.71) deaths attributable to bacterial AMR.

numbers.label: Deaths attributable to bacterial AMR (millions)
numbers.source_quote: there were an estimated 4.95 million (3.62–6.57) deaths associated with bacterial AMR in 2019, including 1.27 million (95% UI 0.911–1.71) deaths attributable to bacterial AMR.

numbers.label: Western sub-Saharan Africa
numbers.source_quote: we estimated the all-age death rate attributable to resistance to be highest in western subSaharan Africa, at 27.3 deaths per 100 000 (20.9–35.3), and lowest in Australasia, at 6.5 deaths (4.3–9.4) per 100 000.

numbers.label: Australasia
numbers.source_quote: we estimated the all-age death rate attributable to resistance to be highest in western subSaharan Africa, at 27.3 deaths per 100 000 (20.9–35.3), and lowest in Australasia, at 6.5 deaths (4.3–9.4) per 100 000.

numbers.label: Deaths associated with resistance, lower respiratory infections
numbers.source_quote: Lower respiratory infections accounted for more than 1.5 million deaths associated with resistance in 2019, making it the most burdensome infectious syndrome.

numbers.label: Attributable deaths from the six leading pathogens (thousands)
numbers.source_quote: were responsible for 929 000 (660 000–1 270 000) deaths attributable to AMR and 3.57 million (2.62–4.78) deaths associated with AMR in 2019.

numbers.label: Share of attributable deaths caused by six pathogens
numbers.source_quote: Six pathogens accounted for 73.4% (95% uncertainty interval 66.9–78.8) of deaths attributable to bacterial AMR.

numbers.label: MRSA attributable deaths (more than, thousands)
numbers.source_quote: One pathogen–drug combination, meticillinresistant S aureus, caused more than 100 000 deaths attributable to AMR in 2019
